maml:description.maml:para: Shows the versions of AD Manager and of its PowerShell engine, the language mode and the connection of this window.

Get-AdmVersion tells which AD Manager and which PowerShell engine this window runs, the language mode (Constrained or Full), and the domain, the domain controller and the account of the connection the window belongs to. It reads nothing from the directory.
None.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets one object of the domain by its identity, or the objects that a ready LDAP filter finds.

Get-AdmObject reads through the connection of this window only (one domain controller; there is no -Server and no -Credential). The identity is a distinguished name, an objectGUID, a SID, a sAMAccountName or a user principal name. The objects are of every kind: each is typed AdMng.Object first (so that the default display is one table), then AdMng.User, AdMng.Group or AdMng.Computer by what it is, and each has the properties ObjectKind and DistinguishedName. Attributes keep their type; the value of a secret that the Attribute Editor never shows is masked. An object that does not exist is a non-terminating error that names it. Results are streamed one object at a time and Stop (Ctrl+C) cancels the read.
The object: a distinguished name, an objectGUID, a SID, a sAMAccountName or a user principal name. Accepts what the pipeline brings: names as text, or objects that have a DistinguishedName.

The distinguished name of the container to search in; the domain by default. Press Tab to complete the naming contexts and the containers this window has already shown. An identity that is a distinguished name is read where it is and ignores -SearchBase.
How deep to search below -SearchBase: Base (the container itself), OneLevel (its direct children) or Subtree (everything below it, the default).

Attributes to return besides the default ones, by LDAP name; press Tab to complete them from the schema. * returns every attribute the account may read. Values keep their type (numbers, booleans, dates in local time, GUIDs, multi-valued attributes as arrays; SIDs as text); secrets that the Attribute Editor never shows are masked.
How many objects the domain controller returns per page (1 to 10000, default 500). The objects are passed on as each page arrives.
The most objects to return. 0, the default, returns all of them.
A ready LDAP filter, for example (&(objectCategory=person)(department=IT)). Its syntax is checked first; a wrong filter is an error before anything is read.
Identities as text, or objects that have a DistinguishedName.
AdMng.Object, AdMng.User, AdMng.Group, AdMng.Computer

maml:description.maml:para: Gets user accounts, by identity or by filters.

Get-AdmUser reads user accounts through the connection of this window. With -Identity it reads the accounts named (a distinguished name, objectGUID, SID, sAMAccountName or user principal name); without it, it searches with the filters of its parameters, all of which must match; a * in a text filter is a wildcard and everything else is literal. Besides the attributes it returns Enabled, LockedOut and UserAccountControlFlags. Results are streamed one object at a time and Stop (Ctrl+C) cancels the read.
The name (name / cn); * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The sAMAccountName; * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The user principal name; * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The first name (givenName); * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The surname (sn); * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The display name; * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The e-mail address (mail); * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The department; * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The job title; * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The company; * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
The description; * is a wildcard, everything else is literal (a bracket, a backslash or a parenthesis in the value belongs to the value).
$true for enabled accounts, $false for disabled ones; both when omitted.
A ready LDAP filter added to the other filters; its syntax is checked first, a wrong filter is an error before anything is read.

Values keep their type (numbers, booleans, dates in local time, GUIDs, multi-valued attributes as arrays; SIDs as text); secrets that the Attribute Editor never shows are masked.
How many objects the domain controller returns per page (1 to 10000, default 500). The objects are passed on as each page arrives.
The most objects to return. 0, the default, returns all of them.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets the members of a group, with -Recursive also those of the groups nested in it.

Get-AdmGroupMember reads the direct members of a group (the values of member, also beyond 1500) through the connection of this window. With -Recursive it lists what the All (nested) list of the program shows: the direct and the indirect members, the domain controller evaluating the nesting (a cycle of groups ends there); the nested groups are listed too, -ExcludeGroups leaves them out. A member that cannot be read (another domain, deleted meanwhile, no permission) is counted in one warning. Results are streamed one object at a time and Stop (Ctrl+C) cancels the read.
The group: a distinguished name, an objectGUID, a SID or a sAMAccountName. Accepts what the pipeline brings: names as text, or objects that have a DistinguishedName.
Also lists the members of the groups nested in the group, to any depth: what the All (nested) list of the program shows. The domain controller evaluates the nesting.
Leaves the groups out of the result: only the accounts and other objects that are members.

Attributes to return besides the default ones, by LDAP name; press Tab to complete them from the schema. * returns every attribute the account may read. maml:description.maml:para: Finds objects of the domain by the value of an attribute, or by a ready LDAP filter.

Search-AdmObject builds the LDAP filter itself from -Name, or from -Attribute and -Value, and escapes every value (RFC 4515): a value such as Łukasz (Kraków)*\ matches only itself, a * in it is a literal star and a value that looks like a filter is only a value. -Match says how a value is compared: Exact (the default), StartsWith, Contains or EndsWith. -Filter takes a ready LDAP filter, whose syntax is checked first. The search does not accept secret attributes. Results are streamed one object at a time and Stop (Ctrl+C) cancels the read.
The name (name) to look for; several names find objects with any of them. A star in the name is a literal star; -Match says how it is compared.
How a value is compared with the attribute: Exact (the default), StartsWith, Contains or EndsWith.
Only objects of this class (user, group, organizationalUnit, ...).

The distinguished name of the container to search in; the domain by default. Press Tab to complete the naming contexts and the containers this window has already shown. An identity that is a distinguished name is read where it is and ignores -SearchBase.
How deep to search below -SearchBase: Base (the container itself), OneLevel (its direct children) or Subtree (everything below it, the default).

Attributes to return besides the default ones, by LDAP name; press Tab to complete them from the schema. * returns every attribute the account may read. Values keep their type (numbers, booleans, dates in local time, GUIDs, multi-valued attributes as arrays; SIDs as text); secrets that the Attribute Editor never shows are masked.
How many objects the domain controller returns per page (1 to 10000, default 500). The objects are passed on as each page arrives.
The most objects to return. 0, the default, returns all of them.
The attribute(s) to compare, by LDAP name; press Tab to complete them from the schema. An object matches when any of the attributes matches any of the values. Secret attributes are refused.
The value(s) to look for. A star or a bracket in a value is part of the value; -Match says how it is compared. Several values find objects that have any of them.
A ready LDAP filter, for example (&(objectCategory=person)(department=IT)). Its syntax is checked first; a wrong filter is an error before anything is read.
None.
AdMng.Object, AdMng.User, AdMng.Group, AdMng.Computer

dev:remarks.maml:para: Finds the groups whose description starts with the text, including its parenthesis and star.

maml:description.maml:para: Shows the objects of the pipeline in a grid of the program.

Out-AdmGrid opens a window with the objects as rows and their properties as columns, the way the lists of the program look: click a column to sort, type in the filter box to narrow the rows, copy the selected rows with Ctrl+C, export them to CSV (formulas are protected), and open an object with Enter or a double-click when the objects have a DistinguishedName. Every value is turned into text before the grid opens, and nothing is written anywhere unless you export from the grid. Like Out-GridView it opens a new window each time.
The objects to show; normally they come from the pipeline. An array is shown row by row.
The title of the grid window. The default is the name of the command.
Any objects.
Nothing is returned.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Shows the users of the department in a grid that can be sorted, filtered, copied and exported. The same with the pipeline: Get-AdmUser -Department IT | Out-AdmGrid.

maml:description.maml:para: Opens the properties of an object in the program.

Open-AdmObject opens the properties window of an object, as a double-click in a list does. The identity is a distinguished name, an objectGUID, a SID, a sAMAccountName or a user principal name. The object is read first through the connection of this window (one domain controller), so a name that does not exist is an error and no window is opened for it. One command opens at most 10 windows.
The object: a distinguished name, an objectGUID, a SID, a sAMAccountName or a user principal name. Accepts what the pipeline brings: names as text, or objects that have a DistinguishedName.
Identities as text, or objects that have a DistinguishedName.
Nothing is returned.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Opens the properties of the account. The same with the pipeline: Get-AdmUser jkowalski | Open-AdmObject.

maml:description.maml:para: Writes the objects of the pipeline to a CSV file, the way the program exports a list.

Export-AdmList writes a CSV file with the properties of the objects as columns. It protects formulas (a value that begins with =, +, - or @ is written so that Excel does not run it), uses the list separator of the regional settings and UTF-8 with a signature, as the list export of the program does. It writes only to the file named in -Path, or to the one you choose in the Save As window when -Path is missing - never to a default place; if you close the window without a file nothing is written. An existing file is replaced only with -Force.
The objects to export; normally they come from the pipeline. An array is written row by row.
The file to write; it is taken literally, so brackets are not wildcards. Without it the Save As window opens and nothing is written until you choose a file.
The field separator, one visible character. The default is the list separator of the regional settings (a semicolon in Poland).
Replaces the file when it exists. Without it an existing file is an error and nothing is written.
Any objects.
The file written and the number of rows and columns.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Writes the users of the department to the file. The same with the pipeline: Get-AdmUser -Department IT | Export-AdmList C:\Temp\it.csv.
